post.title: Quit after a signing bonus? You may repay cash you never got
post.ig:
Quit early, and you may repay bonus money you never got.

Example: a $5,000 bonus prorated over 12 months. Quit at month 6 and you owe $2,500.
After 22% federal withholding and 7.65% Social Security and Medicare, you only received $1,758.75 of that $2,500.
Repay $3,000 or less in a later year and the IRS allows no deduction, so in a 22% bracket that's $550 of tax on money you gave back.
Repaying in the same calendar year lets payroll adjust your wages instead.

Sources: IRS Publication 525 (2025), IRS Publication 15 (2026), One Big Beautiful Bill Act (2025).

post.yt_desc:
Many signing bonuses have a clawback, and many agreements ask for the gross amount back even though taxes were withheld. In this example, quitting halfway through a 12-month, $5,000 bonus means repaying $2,500, of which you only received $1,758.75; repaid in a later year, amounts of $3,000 or less can't be deducted (IRS Publication 525), a rule made permanent in 2025. Sources: IRS Publications 525 and 15.
